overview: 오늘은 위험·안전·헤지 세 축이 모두 대체로 보류로 수렴해 뚜렷한 위험선호/회피 쏠림이 감지되지는 않지만, 성장주 중심의 나스닥은 지속적 매도 신호가 이어지는 반면 광의의 주식과 암호화폐는 보류로 버티는 엇갈림이 나타나 시장 내부 리더십의 약화와 스타일 편중 조정 신호를 시사한다. 안전자산 쪽에서는 국채가 10/22의 단기 매수 신호가 금세 소멸된 뒤 보류로 평형을 유지하고, 금도 어제 매도에서 보류로 완화되는 등 전형적 리스크오프 동조화는 확인되지 않는다. 원자재는 10/16과 10/23에 동시 매수로 보였던 에너지·광범위 상품의 모멘텀이 10/26 이후 보류로 되돌아가 추세 신뢰도가 약해졌고, 그 와중에 천연가스와 농산물만 매도로 남아 섹터 내 비대칭이 두드러진다. 암호화폐는 10/23의 일시적 약세 신호에서 다시 보류로 회복해 기술주 약세와 달리 위험자산군 내부에서도 혼조를 더한다. 종합하면, 최근 며칠 사이 여러 자산이 ‘매수→보류’로 후퇴하고 ‘매도→보류’로 완화되는 상쇄적 전환이 겹치며, 방향성보다는 관망·대기 성격의 중립적 톤이 강화된 단면이다.

news.title: AI Spending Vs. Nasdaq Sell-Off: Why Wall Street May Be Misreading the Boom | Investing.com
news.summary:
Summary:

- The Nasdaq tech sell-off (5.5% weekly drop) is more about funding costs than a collapse in AI demand. With the 10-year yield above 5%, investors question whether AI capex can be financed.
- AI spending remains robust: SpaceX and Meta raised capex plans, and suppliers like TSMC, Lam Research, and ASML reported strong or growing demand. The market is pricing the cost of money, not the end of AI growth.
- Finances matter more than customers: The key constraint is financing and credit quality, not the appetite for AI compute. Five-year CDS spreads show funding risk is highest for highly levered or speculative players (CoreWeave, Oracle to a lesser extent; SpaceX, Meta, Microsoft/Nvidia less affected).
- Capex trajectory: Major cloud builders are projected to rise capex from about $770B in 2024 to ~ $1.2T by 2027, even without counting SpaceX. This suggests ongoing expansion, albeit with tighter selection on marginal projects as credit costs diverge.
- Implication for investors: Returns will depend on credit quality and the ability to monetize new capacity. Fewer marginal projects could lead to tighter capacity and firmer pricing, supporting higher GPU rental rates and more durable growth.

Bottom line: The market’s fears center on funding risk rather than the probability of continued AI buildout. The buildout is not halted; financing conditions will differently affect players, reinforcing a more selective, higher-quality growth path in tech equities.

news.title: Nasdaq Futures Extend Slide as Chip Stocks Fall: Is Weakness Spreading Beyond Tech | Investing.com
news.summary:
Nasdaq tech stock market outlook (as of mid-October): The Nasdaq 100 futures have declined for two straight sessions, pressured by a sharp slide in semiconductor names and concerns over AI spending, memory-chip pricing, and Chinese competition. The broader S&P 500 remains largely flat, creating a key cross-index question: is tech weakness isolated (rotation within tech and a tech-led correction) or a sign of a broader market downturn?

Key levels and signals:
- Immediate support: 30,594–30,600 and 30,594–30,600 for Nasdaq futures; stronger near-term risk if breached.
- Near-term recovery zone: 30,844–30,900; a reclaim suggests selling pressure is waning.
- Important resistance: 31,100–31,290; breaking through would renew attention to prior highs.
- S&P 500 context: ES around 7,834–7,846 support; if ES holds while Nasdaq weakens, it favors sector rotation or tech-specific repricing rather than a broad market collapse.

Bullish case (if the chart holds and recovers):
- Nasdaq holds 30,594–30,600, then moves through 30,844–30,900.
- ES stays above 7,834–7,846; semis stop hitting fresh lows.
- A rally through 31,100–31,290 would strengthen the view that the correction is abating.

Bearish case (if weakness broadens):
- Sustained move below 30,594 and ES below 7,834–7,846.
- Broadening selling could indicate a wider correction ahead of inflation data and earnings season.

Catalysts to watch:
- September CPI (Oct 14) and PPI (Oct 15).
- Semiconductor earnings reports, given the current pressure on chip names.
- Cross-index confirmation: whether Nasdaq weakness persists without S&P downside, or leads ES lower.

Bottom line: The outlook hinges on whether Nasdaq weakness remains contained within tech/semis or spills into the broader market. A hold above key supports would favor rotation/tech repricing; a break below could signal a broader correction.

news.title: Tech Sell-Off: Rotation or Rout? What Traders Need to Know - IG UK
news.summary:
Investors face a tech-led sell-off in October as AI-related capex concerns weigh on valuations. Key points:

- Tech weakness centered in AI/AI infrastructure exposure; Nasdaq and SOX declined sharply in October (Nasdaq -2.6% in one session, SOX down ~15% for the month).
- Year-to-date and spring rally context: SOX up about 60.7% YoY, Nasdaq ~14% YoY, with October pullback retracing only a portion of earlier gains.
- Earnings signals matter: upcoming mega-cap reports are crucial to confirm AI spending translates into revenue/profit. So far, some names (Super Micro, SpaceX) offered relief but sentiment shifted after Meta’s results.
- Risks to watch:
  - Whether AI capex is burning cash faster than it can generate returns, harming chipmakers’ orders.
  - Whether the AI trade’s crowded positioning (broad tech largely exposed to AI spend) eases as new supply returns (e.g., Solidigm) or fresh tech issuance slows.
  - The S&P 500’s tech concentration potentially constraining broader market resilience if defensives don’t compensate.
- Signals to gauge a healthier setup vs. risk of broader rotation:
  - Mega-cap AI revenue growth confirmation from next week’s results.
  - Stabilization or further deterioration in the SOX.
  - Movements in the 10-year yield indicating growth/defensive shifts.
  - Resilience of the S&P 500 alongside reduced appetite for new tech issuances.

Bottom line: If AI spending proves to drive meaningful revenue, October’s pullback could be a healthy reset with a quick re-rotation into tech. If results disappoint, expect a deeper defensive rotation and potential pressure on the broader market.

news.title: Biggest earnings week ahead: Can Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon turn the Nasdaq tide? Or will the ships sink?
news.summary:
Outlook: Nasdaq tech stocks face a pivotal week as earnings from Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon come alongside a market trading below key moving averages.

Key points:
- Technical setup: Nasdaq Composite (around 26,022) and Nasdaq 100 (around 29,037) sit below their 100-day moving averages (26,255 and 29,573 respectively), with 200-day moving averages (24,922 and 27,836) closer below. A sustained move above the 100-day would be a positive signal; continuing dips risk a broader bearish tilt toward the 200-day level.
- Earnings catalysts: Microsoft and Alphabet (Wednesday) and Amazon (Thursday) will test AI/cloud demand, ad economics, AWS growth, and spending efficiency. Guidance on growth and profitability will influence market sentiment more than the results alone.
- Market reaction: Beats don’t guarantee gains; guidance, expectations, and positioning relative to the 100-day average will drive price action. A constructive reaction would require prices to defy the 100-day hurdle and hold above it; failure could reinforce selling pressure toward the 200-day marks.
- Schedule highlights: Major names and sector peers (semiconductors, industrials, energy) are expected to provide clues on demand, margins, and capital spending, with pre-market and post-close reactions shaping the next moves for tech-heavy indices.

Bottom line: The Nasdaq’s near-term trajectory hinges on breaking and sustaining above the 100-day moving averages, supported by strong earnings guidance from Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon. If those reports fail to restore demand or raise doubts about growth, the 200-day levels remain meaningful downside targets.

news.title: Nasdaq 100 forecast: US tech stocks extend decline as AI concerns intensify
news.summary:
Nasdaq tech stock market outlook (as of the latest drop):
- Nasdaq 100 futures extended losses after a hotter-than-expected CPI, with concerns over AI-related valuations and capital-intense AI infrastructure weighing on sentiment.
- Market setup suggests near-term bearishness: price action shows bearish reversal signals, with key support around 29,000–29,240 and resistance at 30,000–30,370; a break below trend line would reinforce downside, next notable level near 29,190.
- Wider backdrop: higher-for-longer rates and inflation fears lift expectations of additional Fed rate hikes (pricing in roughly 45% odds of an Oct hike; ~85% for a Dec hike; plus multiple 25bp hikes over the next year). This increases discounting of future AI-related cash flows.
- Credit-market signal: rising cost to insure US tech debt (record high credit default swap levels for tech) suggests concerns about profitability of the AI capital-spend cycle.
- External drivers: strong TSMC outlook was viewed as not lifting tech broadly, implying market questions about profitability of AI infrastructure despite chip demand.
- Bottom line: the near-term outlook remains cautious to bearish for the Nasdaq 100, with potential for further declines unless AI investment profitability and tech earnings lift sentiment.

news.title: Natural Gas Price Forecast 2026–2027: Henry Hub and TTF Outlook | MarketScreener UAE Emirates
news.summary:
Natural gas price outlook (2026–2027) highlights a split, macro-driven scenario with modestly higher, volatile near-term prices and a softer long term.

Key takeaways:
- Near-term (winter 2026-27): Forecasters anticipate roughly $3.30–$3.50 per MMBtu for Henry Hub this winter, with 2027 common estimates around $3.15–$3.25. The trend aligns with the futures curve; the EIA projects about $3.30 for Q4 2026 and roughly $3.16 for 2027.
- Base case drivers: Storage around 2% above five-year average entering winter; LNG exports near record levels; continued growth in gas production. Weather (El Niño) is a major wild card.
- Cold-winter risk (illustrative): If a cold winter materializes, prices could rebound above $4 as storage is drawn down.
- Mild-winter scenario (illustrative): A warm winter could push prices toward $2.50–$3.00, with the EIA projecting a softer Henry Hub path into 2027.
- 2027 outlook: Overall downward pressure versus 2026 in many forecasts, with the EIA at about $3.16 for 2027. Market expectations vary widely (roughly $3.13–$4.00 depending on forecaster and assumptions).
- Long horizon: Long-term prices are debated; some forecasts imply higher levels into the early 2030s, while others suggest lower structural prices depending on LNG demand, production, and policy.

Strategic implications for macro analysis:
- The price path is highly sensitive to weather (El Niño strength), storage dynamics, and LNG export demand.
- Expect modest average prices in 2026–27 with notable downside/upside risk from weather shocks.
- In the longer term, potential price divergence exists between high-end demand scenarios (LNG, global gas competition) and lower-for-longer scenarios (structural supply growth).

If you want, I can pull the latest EIA forecasts, compare them to major banks’ outlooks, or map a scenario matrix (cold winter vs. mild winter) to quantify potential price paths.

news.title: What Direction Will the Henry Hub Gas Price Take in 2026, 2027? | Rigzone
news.summary:
Summary:
- The EIA’s October Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO) expects the Henry Hub natural gas price to decline in 2026 and 2027, averaging $3.48/MMBtu in 2026 and $3.16/MMBtu in 2027 (down from $3.53/MMBtu in 2025).
- Quarterly forecast highlights: Q4 2026 around $3.30/MMBtu; Q1 2027 about $3.47/MMBtu; Q2 2027 about $2.64/MMBtu; Q3 2027 about $3.04/MMBtu; Q4 2027 about $3.49/MMBtu.
- For 2027, the average is $3.16/MMBtu, down 32 cents from 2026, driven by earlier high January 2026 prices and higher inventories supporting price stability.
- Inventories: forecast end of October 2026 around 3,850 Bcf (2% above five-year average) with build through October; inventories are expected to cushion price upside.
- Temperature and demand context: LNG exports and domestic demand growth, plus ample inventories, limit upside price pressures; prices may dip to a low around $2.60/MMBtu in April–May 2027 before ending the year near $3.90/MMBtu.
- NYMEX/market observations: near-term front-month prices showed volatility, with LNG demand and pipeline constraints supporting physical prices despite softer NYMEX futures; near-term technicals suggest potential testing of support around $3.00/MMBtu with eventual soft pricing over the next 1–2 months.

Bottom line (macro analysis): The 2026–2027 outlook points to a downward trend in Henry Hub prices, moderated by LNG demand and robust inventories, with occasional seasonal volatility but an overall softer pricing environment into 2027.

news.title: Winter weather fuels upside EU LNG demand risk: ACER | S&P Global
news.summary:
Summary for: Winter weather fuels upside EU LNG demand risk: ACER (S&P Global)

- ACER warns EU LNG imports may rise this winter if weather is harsher and gas demand increases, with additional LNG likely to come from the USA.
- EU gas storage is at a record-low for this time of year (74.9% as of Oct 25), heightening reliance on LNG despite a broader decline in overall gas demand since the 2022 crisis.
- Competition for scarce LNG amid Middle East war and Persian Gulf supply disruptions could push Europe and Asia toward higher spot prices and volatility.
- The EU’s gas demand is about 20% lower than during the 2022 crisis, which increases the value of existing storage; weather-driven demand will shape storage evolution.
- Wartime factors have raised the cost of gas injections; estimated upper bound to refill storage this year is €27 billion, with EU outlays totaling €18–€33 billion extra on imports due to the war.
- Global LNG prices have spiked; DES Northwest Europe LNG benchmark around $31.16/MMBtu (as of Oct 26).
- Structural shifts: reduced Qatar LNG and greater US reliance, with the EU receiving roughly 30% of its gas from LNG sources; Russian gas accounts for about 11%, with LNG/pipeline flows down modestly year over year.
- EU policy note: ban on all Russian LNG imports starting 2027 and all Russian pipeline gas imports from autumn 2027.

Bottom line for natural gas price outlook: ACER indicates potential upside risk to EU LNG demand and near-term prices if a harsh winter materializes, driven by record-low storage, elevated import costs from war-related dynamics, and competition for limited LNG, particularly from the USA.

news.title: Natural Gas Heading into Winter 2026 and What Oil and Gas Investors Should Watch | DW Energy Group
news.summary:
Summary: Natural Gas Price Outlook Macro Analysis

- Supply and inventories: U.S. natural gas starts winter 2026 with solid inventories (EIA end-Oct 2026 ~3,850 Bcf, ~2% above five-year average) and rising domestic production (EIA 2026: ~112.2 Bcf/d; 2027: ~116.1 Bcf/d). Strong supply base provides cushion during colder periods.
- Demand and heating: Winter demand remains the key driver. EIA assumes heating demand near last winter and ~1% below the five-winter average, with potential for larger withdrawals if prolonged cold occurs.
- LNG exports: U.S. LNG exports rising (EIA 2026 ~17.6 Bcf/d; 2027 ~18.6 Bcf/d; H1 2026 avg 17.4 Bcf/d, +23% vs. H1-2025). Export expansion supports domestic price dynamics and storage draws, but also links prices to global LNG demand.
- Prices and volatility: Henry Hub is forecast to average about $3.48/MMBtu in 2026, with ~$3.16 in 2027. Prices are sensitive to weather, storage draws, and supply disruptions; extreme cold or supply shocks can spike prices (e.g., Jan 2026 spike to $7.72/MMBtu).
- Weather as a primary variable: El Niño factors (strong likelihood of very strong El Niño in 2026-2027) can influence regional temperatures and consumption, making weekly forecasts and storage data crucial for pricing.
- Investment implications: For gas projects and equities, key drivers are:
  - Production growth and cost structures/subsurface performance
  - LNG export capacity and term contracts
  - Storage draw pace and winter weather risk
  - Policy/regulatory environment and infrastructure developments
  - Commodity price backdrop (base case ~3.5 $/MMBtu in 2026, potential volatility around weather shocks)

Bottom line: The 2026–27 natural gas outlook combines healthy supply and expanding LNG exports with weather-driven demand risk. Prices are likely to remain range-bound with potential for upside spikes during cold spells or supply disruptions, while a robust production base and growing LNG demand support a constructive longer-term trend. Investors should monitor weekly storage draws, LNG export trends, and weather developments (El Niño impacts) alongside production costs and project economics.

news.title: US natural gas futures extend slide as milder forecasts… · Aephel
news.summary:
Natural gas price outlook (macro-focused): US natgas futures fell about 5.8% on Oct 21–23, 2026 as near-term heating demand waned due to milder weather forecasts. The move is weather-driven rather than supply-driven, implying only a modest, disinflationary effect on energy-related inflation. Key takeaways:
- The decline reflects revised temperature outlooks reducing heating demand; crude prices are influenced by different drivers.
- Macroeconomic sensitivity: weaker gas supports a softer energy component in the CPI and may help utility inflation risk, with bond markets reacting to broader risk-off moves.
- What to watch: upcoming temperature outlook revisions (colder updates could lift demand and reverse the decline). Also monitor US energy-inflation link via energy’s share in CPI, and monetary policy expectations (especially if the 10Y yield stays under recent levels).
- Context: Gas was one of the weakest performers among commodities on the latest day; other energy assets moved less in tandem.

news.title: Arable Market Report – 26 October 2026 | AHDB
news.summary:
AHDB Arable Market Report (26 Oct 2026) — Key outlook for agricultural commodities

- UK wheat: Feed wheat prices fell last week, with Nov-2026 at £193.75/t, down £11.25/t. Prices remain below the 20-day moving average and RSI indicates oversold conditions, implying near-term downside risk.
- Global grain drivers: Markets declined as global supply prospects improved and US harvest progress resumed, despite some support from Black Sea disruption and firm crude oil. Russia–Ukraine peace-talk hopes also influenced sentiment.
- U.S. and Europe: Chicago wheat and maize fell significantly (wheat ~6.5%, maize ~3.9%); Paris milling wheat down ~4%. Dry conditions in key U.S. states aided fieldwork and winter wheat planting, with favorable Midwest weather supporting maize harvest. Anticipated USDA progress report due later.
- Black Sea / exports: Shifts in Russian export routes (Baltic Sea) prompted higher Russia wheat export forecasts, affecting global supply dynamics.
- Oilseeds: Soya and canola prices declined on improved U.S. harvest weather and late-week crude price support; ongoing war-related disruptions keep some volatility in sunflower oil and rapeseed via Black Sea trade.
- Crude oil: Brent crude rose to $116.72/bbl, highest since April, supporting some commodity price volatility.
- UK supply/demand outlook (2026/27): AHDB estimates suggest tighter wheat and barley supply offsets; wheat sees lower opening stocks and higher import reliance, while barley faces the tightest balance due to very low production (lowest since 2012/13).
- Market verdict: Near-term downside momentum in grains amid favorable harvest progress and improving supply prospects; the market remains sensitive to Black Sea developments and geopolitical risk, with macro factors (oil, weather) adding volatility. Expect continued downward pressure if US harvest, weather, and global supply signals persist.

news.title: Australian crop margins remain under pressure, but yields provide some relief – News Hub
news.summary:
Summary:

- Rabobank’s Field Crop Margin Outlook 2027 says global crop margins will recover slowly and unevenly through 2027, with ample world supplies limiting sustained price gains. Fertiliser and crop protection costs are expected to rise again.
- Australia: 2027 margins remain pressured by high input costs (fertiliser, diesel, freight) and potential El Niño effects in eastern Australia. Strong yields in Victoria, South Australia, and Western Australia help spread fixed costs over larger outputs and may offset some pressure. In Queensland and northern NSW, drier conditions could erode margins and affect crop mix.
- Local dynamics: Australia saw 2026 margins below historical levels due to high global grain production and elevated input costs from geopolitical disruptions, prompting some farmers to cut fertiliser use and shift from wheat to lower-input crops. Canola remains relatively stable but requires higher investment.
- Short-term measures: Some growers pre-purchased fertiliser and expanded on-farm diesel storage to mitigate supply risk, increasing working capital needs.
- Global outlook: Margin recovery depends on weather, geopolitics, and crop fundamentals. El Niño persists into early 2027, adding uncertainty. US margins remain vulnerable, Europe could recover if yields normalise, Brazil maintains healthier margins for soy/corn, and Argentina’s soybean margins may improve but corn margins stay exposed to fertiliser costs and taxation.

news.title: Crops analysis | Grains collectively carve fresh near-term lows - Pro Farmer
news.summary:
Here’s a concise outlook based on Pro Farmer’s crops analysis:

- Corn: Prices slipped to near multi-month lows (Dec corn at about $4.48-4.50). Technical selling dominated, with lower wheat/soybeans dampening appetite for corn. U.S. harvest rapid (60% harvested vs 44% prior week; 66% avg). Hedge selling by commercials increasing. Brazil/Argentina production unchanged per Pro Farmer (Brazil 140 MMT, Argentina 60 MMT). U.S. harvest pace and favorable near-term weather in the U.S. Corn Belt support the bearish tone; Brazil's weather remains variable, with upcoming rainfall in some regions.

- Soybeans and meal: Soybeans weaker (Jan soybeans ~ $12.43), closing near a two-month low; meal ~ $334.60, near two-month low; oil ~ 66.71 cents/lb. Ongoing technical selling and stronger Brazilian competition (real weakness) pressuring U.S. prices. Soybean harvest progressing; some weather concerns in Brazil (excess rain in south, dryness in central/northeast). Cordonnier left 2026-27 Brazil soy at 182 MMT and Argentina at 54 MMT.

- Wheat: Winter wheat prices lower (SRW ~ $6.10 1/4; HRW ~$6.50 1/2; both near 3.5-month lows). Technical selling persists; lower corn/soybeans weigh on wheat. Russia-Ukraine peace prospects continue to cap buying interest. U.S. winter wheat plantings 77% complete (vs 5-year avg), still behind.

- Cotton: Declined (Dec cotton ~ 78.06 cents). Broader grain selloff contributing to cotton weakness after a recent range breakout.

- Overall factors driving near-term sentiment:
  - Broad-based technical selling and export competitiveness shifts (Brazilian corn/soybeans pressure U.S. prices).
  - U.S. harvest progress providing hedge selling pressure, especially in corn and soybeans.
  - Mixed weather signals: favorable near-term U.S. harvest weather; variable Brazil weather with localized concerns.
  - Grain weakness contributing to downstream softness in cotton.

If you want, I can tailor this to a specific commodity or time horizon (e.g., next 2 weeks vs. next 1–2 months) or pull out key support/resistance levels.

news.title: Sugar, wheat, soybean prices hit multi-week lows as supply outlook improves - CNBC TV18
news.summary:
Summary:
- The article notes a near-term correction in agricultural commodities as sugar, wheat, and soybean futures fall to multi-week lows due to improved supply outlooks: better crop estimates, favorable weather (especially in Brazil), stronger crop expectations from Australia, Argentina, and Canada, and Russia exploring alternate shipment routes.
- Despite the pullbacks, year-to-date and year-on-year inflation in agricultural commodities remains elevated. Factors sustaining higher-longer-term levels include geopolitical tensions, input costs (fuels, fertilizers), and energy-market transmissions.
- Specifics:
  - Sugar: about a 5.5% drop to a two-month low, aided by lower crude oil, a weaker Brazilian real, and better Brazilian weather.
  - Wheat: down to a 15-week low helped by Russian alternate routes and otherwise supportive crop outlooks from other regions.
  - Soybeans: near a two-month low after a US report suggesting a record crop increase (roughly 1% year-over-year, ~7% from last year).
  - Other notes: coffee and palm oil also easing; overall 2026 remains higher vs. prior years despite monthly declines in some commodities.
- Bottom line for market outlook: near-term corrections are ongoing as supply risks ease, but the broader 2026 agricultural inflation backdrop remains elevated; long-term demand and geopolitical developments will continue to influence prices.

news.title: Grain market review: Coarse grains | World Grain
news.summary:
Summary:

- The global maize (corn) market shifted from a recent peak to a softer tone after an October USDA production forecast surprised to the upside. The IGC notes a 6% drop in its world price index and a 10% month-on-month fall in nearby US futures, driven by larger-than-expected quarterly stocks and USDA’s higher 2026-27 yield/production estimates, along with wet harvests and disease pressures weighing on price support.
- Regional price moves: Argentina Up River prices fell to $213 fob; Brazil Paranagua at $225 fob. US Gulf export quotes down $16–$23, to about $229 fob. Sorghum futures weakened in the US Gulf by $16 fob; Argentina Up River sorghum rose to $225 fob; Australian sorghum up to $320 fob (Brisbane).
- Barley eased about 1% on modest EU/Australia declines, with French EU export values soft and Black Sea prices modestly higher on supply expectations.
- Demand dynamics: Despite softer prices, strong export demand remains a key support theme, with record pace in some shipments for the current marketing year.
- Policy/production context: AHDB notes USDA raised US maize production estimates to 407.3 million tonnes, signaling a large US crop and pressuring futures. In Europe, FranceAgriMer indicates EU maize production at the lowest since 1994, implying higher EU imports (forecast up to 25 million tonnes) and significantly lower exports (down ~37%).
- Global price backdrop: FAO’s Food Price Index for maize rose 5.6% in September amid tightening supply prospects; sorghum and barley prices also rose in September, reflecting broader feed-grain demand and expectations of increased Chinese purchases.

Bottom line: While prices have cooled from late-September highs due to optimistic US production outlooks, tightening supply signals in the EU and ongoing strong export demand continue to support some price strength in select regions and grain types.
